monitoring.why_p1: This "used" RAM is kernel page cache — files already read from disk and kept in memory to avoid reading them again. It is not memory allocated by any process; it is free RAM put to good use.
monitoring.why_p2: When a program requests more memory, the kernel reclaims this cache instantly and automatically before ever touching swap. Manually purging it only degrades performance by forcing subsequent disk reads.
monitoring.why_note: Linux manages memory intelligently. Unused RAM is wasted RAM.
